STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate. It has a flat centre with a raised rim band and no inner wall, so it is a **flat plate (square)**.

STEP 2 - Scale: The plate spans about 340 px across its diagonal-free width in the image. Square plates are 20-30 cm, so I take 24 cm as the width. Pixels per cm is about 340 / 24 = 14.2 px/cm. No reference object of known size is clearly visible, so this is the least certain number.

STEP 3 - Food item: The food is a soft, white, crumbly fresh cheese (paneer-like), in four irregular pieces.
- Footprint, from the visible patches (top blob ~150x130 px, left crumbles ~170x180 px, bottom wedge ~130x180 px, right wedge ~110x140 px), each at about 60% coverage: total ≈ 53,000 px². At 14.2 px/cm, that is about 260 cm².
- Thickness: pieces are about 2 cm thick at their peak, and mounds average about half their peak, so about 1 cm average.
- Volume ≈ 260 cm² × 1.0 cm ≈ 260 ml. Density 1.0 g/ml gives about 260 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No base layer is visible under the cheese, and the plate is otherwise empty. No extra items.

STEP 5 - Energy: Fresh cheese (paneer-like) is about 300 kcal per 100 g.

Estimated total: about 260 g, about 780 kcal. The main uncertainty is the plate width and the average thickness.
